question: The EU and India have negotiated a free trade agreement. On 11 September 2026, the Commission submitted to the Council its proposals for signature and conclusion of the agreement. The agreement facilitates the temporary entry into the EU of Indian nationals providing services, including in the IT sector, and intra-corporate transferees.

The EU and India also plan to recruit staff through the EU Talent Pool and the EU office set up in India in February 2026. In addition, their 2030 cooperation agenda envisages increasing student exchanges and facilitating the recognition of qualifications. Graduates from India can stay in the EU after their studies to look for a job.

The economic analysis of the agreement published by the Commission does not estimate how many workers might come from India, nor how their arrival would affect employment and wages in the EU and in individual Member States. 1.

How many Indian nationals can take up employment or provide services in the EU under the provisions of the agreement, the EU Talent Pool, the activities of the office in India and the post-study residence scheme – broken down by country, sector and basis for residence?
Has the Commission assessed the impact of the arrival of these people and the possible increase in services provided from India on employment and wages in Polish IT and business services centres?
Before the European Parliament votes on its consent to the agreement, will the Commission supplement its analysis to include these impacts? If not, why not?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.11.2026) Under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Member States retain the right to determine volumes of admission of third-country nationals to their territory to seek work1. Issuing visas also remains a competence of the Member States.

This competence remains intact under the EU-India Free Trade Agreement2, the EU Talent Pool3 and the EU Legal Gateway Office pilot and all other initiatives on labour mobility. These initiatives also do not affect the rights of Member States to carry out labour market test before allowing international recruitment.
The Impact Assessment for the EU Talent Pool assessed the economic impacts, benefits for the enterprises and estimated the number of successful matches between jobseekers and employers4.

Furthermore, the Council Conclusions on the new Strategic EU-India Agenda of 20 October 20255 welcomed the strong impetus in relations between the EU and India and endorsed the Joint Communication on a ‘New Strategic EU-India Agenda’6.

The Council welcomed increased efforts to promote and facilitate orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility procedures for skilled professionals between the EU and India through new, targeted initiatives, such as the European Legal Gateway Office pilot7, aimed at greater connectivity of labour markets, while respecting national competences.
1 Article 79(5) of the TFEU. 2 Proposal for a Council Decision on the signing of the Free Trade Agreement between the European Union and
